You’re currently at a clean handoff point: there’s a recorded **Current Champion** (`baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`), **no PASS candidates**, and **nothing INCONCLUSIVE**. The next step is simply to run the queued automation commands in order.

## What to do next (run in order)

```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```

## What each command will produce

1) **`aub_autopilot.py ... --select-best`**
- Runs module-level candidate experiments from `module_registry.yaml`
- Scores them against your evaluation (where your “tuning” and “lockbox” stats come from)
- If anything beats the champion with your selection rules, it should mark/select a new best candidate (or at least produce a report explaining why none passed)

2) **`system_autopilot.py ... --run`**
- Runs system-level candidates defined in `system_candidates.yaml`
- This is usually where integration/stack-level changes are tested after module exploration

3) **`aub_next_fix.py ... --output .../next_fix.md`**
- Generates a “what to fix next” plan based on the latest run results
- Writes to: `baseline/reports/next_fix.md`

## Quick sanity checks after running
- Confirm whether a new champion file was written/updated (or whether it explicitly says “no candidate passed”)
- Skim the latest reports for:
  - regressions on **lockbox_min** (often treated as a safety floor)
  - improvements on **tuning_mean** without collapsing **tuning_min**

If you paste the console output (or the generated report paths), I can help interpret why candidates did/didn’t pass and what the next fix plan is targeting.
